images.title: A cell is named by column and row
images.purpose: Shows that the cell where column E meets row 5 is called E5 and holds 42.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. A small spreadsheet grid centred, one column and one row tinted so they cross at one cell.
images.exact_structure: A spreadsheet grid of 5 columns and 5 rows of equal white cells with thin grey (#6B7280) lines, plus a grey header row above and a grey header column at the left. Only one column header shows text, E, over the fifth column, and only one row header shows text, 5, beside the fifth row; the other header cells are blank. Column E is lightly tinted teal (#0072B2) and row 5 lightly tinted amber (#E69F00); they cross at the bottom right cell, which has a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) border and holds the number 42. A small tag pointing to that cell reads E5. All other cells are empty.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The column letter and the row number together name a cell.
images.description: Shows that the cell where column E meets row 5 is called E5 and holds 42.
images.context: Farooq's Mathematics marks, 42, in cell E5.

image_decisions.why: The crossing column and row make the naming rule for a cell visible.
